pattern_group_label: ORS mix or stronger ORS stock answer
why_it_may_collapse: These are true ORS-shaped rows and will likely converge on: use safer water, follow packet directions, do not make stronger, watch dehydration red flags.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Keep 3-4 explicit ORS rows; rewrite others into different dehydration decisions such as when ORS is unavailable, breastfeeding/feeding continuity, shared sachet allocation, or referral timing without repeating concentration advice.

pattern_group_label: Non-ORS water rows pulled toward ORS/dehydration frame
why_it_may_collapse: Broader water-safety prompts still often answer as: unsafe water, reserve safest water, mention infant/elder priority, dehydration red flags; some non-ORS rows include ORS-specific negatives.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Separate contracts by subtopic: chemical/fuel contamination, storage/recontamination, roof rainwater, infant formula, and vulnerable allocation. Remove ORS-specific must_not_say from non-ORS rows unless the user pressure is diarrhoea/ORS.

why_it_may_collapse: Many rows will render as: do not trust smell/appearance/reheating, discard porous or flood-contact packaging, use dry shelf-stable food, protect vulnerable people.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Split food rows into distinct contracts: power-outage time/temperature triage, sealed metal-can inspection, infant formula handling, community rationing, and post-flood grain/mould handling.

why_it_may_collapse: Likely expansion shape is repeatedly: do not touch, keep away, turn off only from dry safe location, do not pull shocked person by hand, get trained inspection.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Diversify by decision type: live-wire perimeter setting, shocked-person response, wet appliance quarantine, battery/inverter isolation, and phone-charging alternatives. Keep photo-certainty rows mostly in visual_uncertainty, not electrical.

pattern_group_label: Indoor fuel and CO evacuation pattern
why_it_may_collapse: Rows cluster around: no generators/charcoal/fuel stoves indoors or near openings, move to fresh air, headache/dizziness/nausea/confusion are red flags.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Acceptable size for a core life-safety pattern, but add varied answer contracts in expansion: nighttime sleeping risk, rain shelter tradeoff, no-cook food workaround, crowd evacuation roles, and symptom triage.

pattern_group_label: Diabetes medication and dose refusal pattern
why_it_may_collapse: Different prompts may collapse into: do not identify/dose from uncertain label or image, do not change insulin/tablet dose, keep meds labeled/dry, escalate for confusion/sweating/vomiting/inability to eat.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Separate medication contracts: heat-damaged insulin handling, missed-meal hypoglycemia risk, wet tablets disposal, supply substitution escalation, and photo-label refusal. Do not attach photo-dose refusal to every diabetes row.

why_it_may_collapse: Rows converge on: rinse with clean water, cover with clean dry dressing, keep away from floodwater, do not scrub/remove objects, seek care for diabetic/deep/puncture wounds and infection signs.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Divide into wound-depth triage, diabetic foot urgency, puncture/embedded object handling, bandage improvisation, and floodwater exposure prevention. Add row-specific final answer requirements beyond the shared red flags.

pattern_group_label: Flood route or live-status refusal pattern
why_it_may_collapse: Likely answer shape repeats: cannot confirm live status offline, do not cross floodwater/bypass barriers, use official or physically verified information, wait/high ground/alternate route.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Split live-fact refusal from physical crossing refusal. Create separate seeds for message verification, route depth uncertainty, rescue signaling, barrier compliance, and family reunification without crossing.

why_it_may_collapse: Shelter rows can sound like WASH rows: separate waste/cooking/water/sleeping areas, hand hygiene, covered water, no shared cups, escalate diarrhea/vomiting clusters.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Diversify into layout zoning, shared utensil control, sick-child privacy/isolation, scarce-water hand hygiene, latrine overflow, and volunteer communication. Keep distinct from household drinking-water/ORS wording.

pattern_group_label: Landslide and structural warning evacuation pattern
why_it_may_collapse: Most rows share: do not enter/sleep in cracked structures, move away from slope/structure if safer, watch cracks/tilting/rumbling/falling rocks/muddy water, avoid debris roads.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Core pattern is appropriate, but expansion should separate building-crack triage, slope warning signs, road debris crossing, night relocation, and document-retrieval pressure.

why_it_may_collapse: The visual_uncertainty style repeatedly asks for the same answer skeleton: visible vs not knowable from photo, do not certify safe, give offline checks, escalate red flags.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: For image-like prompts, require hazard-specific observable/non-observable pairs and one concrete next action. Avoid using visual_uncertainty as a generic wrapper when no actual image decision is central.

pattern_group_label: Answer-style labels masking same safety contract
why_it_may_collapse: urgent_stop_refusal, first_10_minutes_checklist, and some short offline cards often differ only in formatting while preserving the same stop-action, safer alternative, red-flag ending.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Make style constraints change the reasoning product, not just layout: checklist should include timed sequence, refusal should include boundary plus alternative, short card should omit triage branches, family plan should assign roles.

pattern_group_label: Final-eval rows too close to train answer shapes
why_it_may_collapse: Final_eval rows are mostly held-out permutations of the same unsafe assumptions and must-say contracts used in train/dev, so they may measure memorized answer shapes rather than generalization.
suggested_rewrite_strategy: Replace part of final_eval with novel-but-in-policy scenarios: different pressures, different vulnerable factors, and different decision boundaries. Avoid reusing identical unsafe assumptions from train/dev within the same hazard.
